records.subject: Vacancy-doped Fe3−x−ΔGaxO4 gallium ferrites
records.object: Fraction of Ga3+ ions occupying octahedral B sites
records.quote: The magnetic after-effect (MAE) spectra of vacancy-doped (Delta) gallium ferrites: Fe3-x-DeltaGaxO4 (0.05 less than or equal to x less than or equal to 1.0; Delta approximate to 5 x 10(-3)) are studied in the temperature range 4.4 K < T < 460 K.
context_quotes: Our analysis reveals that for all investigated concentrations, x, a certain fraction of Ga3+ ions is substituted on octahedral (B) sites of the spinel lattice, thereby interfering strongly with the magnetite-specific charge transport mechanisms: (i) electron tunnelling (4 K < T < 35 K) is suppressed for all Ga contents x; (ii) wide-range electron hopping (50 K < T < 125 K) only occurs, in modified form, for 0.05 less than or equal to x < 0.4; (iii) the Verwey transition (T-V approximate to 125 K), too, is affected and finally suppressed (x greater than or equal to 0.4); (iv) the vacancy-mediated ionic relaxations, peaks III (approximate to 300 K) and II (approximate to 380 K), are reduced in strength and temperature-shifted with increasing Ga-3+ contents.
records.conditions: MAE analysis; all investigated x from 0.05 to 1.0; Δ approximately 5×10−3.

records.subject: Bilayer sandwich nanocellulose-salt engineering with other anions and cations
records.conditions: Relative to LiCl-nanocellulose bilayer engineering.
records.quote: We discover that the sandwiched LiCl-nanocellulose-engineered paper promises an ion-transport junction between the negatively and positively charged bilayer polyelectrolytes for application in MEGs with both high voltage and high current outputs.
context_quotes: Moreover, we demonstrated the universality of this bilayer sandwich nanocellulose-salt engineering strategy with other anions and cations, exhibiting similar power generation ability, indicating that it could be the next generation of sustainable MEGs with low cost, easier operation, and high performance.

records.subject: Inferior ionic conductivity and poor hierarchical structure design
records.conditions: Traditional moisture-induced power devices operating in the ambient environment.
records.quote: However, the present moisture-induced power devices traditionally generate intermittent or bursts of energy, especially for much lower current outputs (generally keeping at nA or mu A levels) from the ambient environment, typically suffering from inferior ionic conductivity and poor hierarchical structure design for manipulating sustained air water and ion-charge transport.
